issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodos function. User input 'keyword' is directly interpolated into SQL query using template literals without any sanitization or parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: `const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2'; const rows = await db.query(query, [`%${keyword}%`, `%${keyword}%`]);`

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus function. User input 'completed' is concatenated directly into SQL query without validation or parameterization. An attacker could inject arbitrary SQL code.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries and validate input type: `if (typeof completed !== 'boolean' && completed !== 'true' && completed !== 'false') throw new Error('Invalid status'); const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [completed === 'true' || completed === true]);`

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser function. User input 'userId' is directly embedded in SQL query using template literals without sanitization or parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: `const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);`

issues.description: HTML entity encoding for XSS prevention is insufficient. This approach only handles basic cases and may not prevent all XSS attacks, especially in different contexts (JavaScript, URL, CSS).
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested library like DOMPurify or implement context-aware sanitization. Consider if sanitization is needed at all if data is properly escaped at the presentation layer. For database storage, store raw data and sanitize only on output.

issues.description: Weak ID generation using Date.now() and Math.random(). This can lead to collisions in high-concurrency scenarios and predictable IDs that could be security risks.
issues.suggestion: Use a proper UUID library: `import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid'; function generateId(): string { return uuidv4(); }` or use database auto-increment/sequences.

issues.description: Storing sanitized HTML entities in the database violates separation of concerns. Sanitization should occur at the presentation layer, not the data layer. This makes data harder to search and reuse.
issues.suggestion: Remove sanitization before database storage. Store raw validated data: `const todo: Todo = { id: generateId(), title: input.title.trim(), description: input.description || '', completed: false, createdAt: new Date() };` Apply sanitization only when rendering to HTML.

issues.description: getAllTodos retrieves all todos without pagination. This will cause performance issues and memory problems as the dataset grows.
issues.suggestion: Add pagination parameters: `export async function getAllTodos(limit: number = 50, offset: number = 0): Promise<{ todos: Todo[], total: number }> { const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2'; const countQuery = 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM todos'; const [rows, countResult] = await Promise.all([db.query(query, [limit, offset]), db.query(countQuery)]); return { todos: rows as Todo[], total: countResult[0].count }; }`

issues.description: updateTodoStatus does not check if the todo exists before updating. It silently succeeds even if no rows are affected, which could mask bugs.
issues.suggestion: Verify the update affected a row: `const result = await db.query(query, [completed, id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new Error('Todo not found'); }`

issues.description: deleteTodo does not check if the todo exists before deletion. It silently succeeds even if no rows are deleted.
issues.suggestion: Verify the deletion affected a row: `const result = await db.query(query, [id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new Error('Todo not found'); } return result.rowCount;`

issues.description: getTodoById does not validate the id parameter. While parameterized queries prevent SQL injection, invalid IDs should be validated for better error handling.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: `if (!id || typeof id !== 'string' || id.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Invalid todo ID'); }`

issues.description: Error handling in createTodo throws a generic error message. More specific error messages would improve debugging and API responses.
issues.suggestion: Throw more specific errors: `if (!input.title || input.title.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Title is required'); } if (input.title.length > 200) { throw new Error('Title must be 200 characters or less'); }`

issues.description: Database query in createTodo does not handle potential race conditions or database errors gracefully. No transaction handling for atomic operations.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling and consider transactions: `try { await db.query(query, params); return todo; } catch (error) { if (error.code === '23505') { throw new Error('Duplicate todo ID'); } throw new Error('Failed to create todo: ' + error.message); }`

issues.description: validateTodoInput returns boolean instead of throwing errors with specific messages. This makes it harder to provide meaningful feedback to users about what exactly is invalid.
issues.suggestion: Consider throwing descriptive errors or returning a validation result object: `type ValidationResult = { valid: boolean; errors: string[] }; export function validateTodoInput(input: CreateTodoInput): ValidationResult { const errors: string[] = []; if (!input.title || input.title.trim().length === 0) errors.push('Title is required'); if (input.title.length > 200) errors.push('Title too long'); return { valid: errors.length === 0, errors }; }`

issues.description: Missing error types/classes for domain-specific errors. Using generic Error makes it harder to handle different error scenarios appropriately.
issues.suggestion: Define custom error classes: `export class TodoNotFoundError extends Error { constructor(id: string) { super(`Todo with id ${id} not found`); this.name = 'TodoNotFoundError'; } } export class InvalidTodoInputError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'InvalidTodoInputError'; } }`

issues.description: No database connection pooling or query optimization strategy is evident. Consider indexing created_at column for ORDER BY performance.
issues.suggestion: Ensure database indexes exist: Add migration for `CREATE INDEX idx_todos_created_at ON todos(created_at DESC);` and `CREATE INDEX idx_user_todos_user_id ON user_todos(user_id);`

issues.description: searchTodos uses LIKE with leading wildcards (%keyword%) which prevents index usage and causes full table scans. This will be very slow on large datasets.
issues.suggestion: Consider full-text search capabilities: Use PostgreSQL full-text search with GIN indexes: `CREATE INDEX idx_todos_fulltext ON todos USING GIN(to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || description)); const query = "SELECT * FROM todos WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || description) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)"; const rows = await db.query(query, [keyword]);`

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES DETECTED: This file contains three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in the newly added functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) that must be fixed immediately. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, potentially leading to data theft, modification, or deletion. Additionally, the file has medium-severity issues including weak ID generation, improper data sanitization placement, missing pagination causing performance problems, and inadequate error handling. While the existing CRUD functions (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) correctly use parameterized queries, the three new search functions critically fail to follow these security best practices. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED: Replace all string concatenation and template literal SQL queries with parameterized queries.

testCoverage.summary: ZERO test coverage exists for src/todo.ts. All 11 exported functions are completely untested. This is especially critical because 3 NEW functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) contain INTENTIONAL SQL injection vulnerabilities that must be caught by security tests. Priority testing needed: (1) SQL injection tests for the 3 vulnerable functions to demonstrate exploitability, (2) XSS prevention in sanitizeInput, (3) Input validation edge cases in validateTodoInput, (4) Database error handling across all async functions, (5) Parameterized query verification for secure functions (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo). The validation and sanitization functions are security-critical and require comprehensive edge-case testing. Recommend creating src/todo.test.ts with at least 45 test cases covering all identified gaps.

suggestions.description: Extract SQL query building logic into a QueryBuilder pattern to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities and eliminate code duplication across all query functions
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates SQL injection vulnerabilities, centralizes query logic, makes testing easier, provides consistent parameterized queries, and enforces type safety (completed should be boolean, not string)

suggestions.description: Use parameterized queries with proper type conversion instead of string concatenation/interpolation
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection attacks, maintains consistency with other functions in the file, properly types searchTodosByStatus parameter as boolean instead of string, and follows the established pattern already used in createTodo, getTodoById, etc.

suggestions.description: Modernize validation logic using optional chaining and early returns with descriptive error messages
suggestions.benefits: Uses optional chaining for safer property access, provides specific error messages for better debugging, makes validation results more informative, and allows consumers to display user-friendly error messages

suggestions.description: Extract sanitization logic into a dedicated function to handle both title and description consistently
suggestions.benefits: Encapsulates sanitization logic, makes it reusable for update operations, improves testability, and clarifies the sanitization step in the createTodo flow

suggestions.description: Use destructuring and modern object construction for cleaner code
suggestions.benefits: Uses destructuring with default values for cleaner parameter handling, makes the relationship between todo properties and query parameters more explicit, and reduces intermediate variable assignments

suggestions.description: Extract common database query pattern into a Repository pattern for better separation of concerns
suggestions.benefits: Separates data access logic from business logic, makes database operations easier to test and mock, provides a single point to manage all database interactions, and allows for easier migration to an ORM later

refactorings.summary: Found 10 refactoring opportunities with 2 high-impact, 5 medium-impact, and 3 low-impact suggestions. Critical issues: (1) The three newly added search functions have severe SQL injection vulnerabilities that must be fixed by using parameterized queries; (2) searchTodosByStatus has incorrect type (string instead of boolean); (3) Multiple opportunities to introduce Repository/QueryBuilder patterns to centralize database logic and reduce duplication; (4) Validation can be improved to return descriptive error messages; (5) Sanitization logic should be extracted and enhanced; (6) Several modernization opportunities exist including destructuring, optional chaining, and better error handling. The code follows good practices with async/await and parameterized queries in older functions, but the new functions break this pattern and introduce security vulnerabilities.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED: Fix SQL injection vulnerabilities in all three newly added search functions. Replace string concatenation and template literal SQL queries with parameterized queries using $1, $2 placeholders and passing user input as separate parameters to db.query().

Fix incorrect parameter type in searchTodosByStatus function. The 'completed' parameter should be boolean, not string. Update function signature to: searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]>

Create comprehensive test suite for src/todo.ts with at least 45 test cases. Priority: SQL injection tests demonstrating vulnerabilities in searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, and getTodosByUser; XSS prevention tests for sanitizeInput; validation edge cases; and parameterized query verification for existing secure functions.
Add input validation for all search functions. Validate keyword length, userId format, and ensure completed parameter is properly typed as boolean before executing queries.

Implement Repository or QueryBuilder pattern to centralize database query logic, enforce parameterized queries consistently, and improve testability. This will prevent future SQL injection vulnerabilities.
Replace weak ID generation (Date.now() + Math.random()) with cryptographically secure UUID generation using crypto.randomUUID() or the uuid library to prevent collisions and predictable IDs.

Remove HTML sanitization from database storage layer. Store raw validated data and apply sanitization only at the presentation layer. This improves data searchability, reusability, and follows separation of concerns principles.
Add pagination to getAllTodos function with limit and offset parameters to prevent memory issues and performance degradation as the dataset grows. Return both paginated results and total count.

Improve error handling across all functions: (1) Update validateTodoInput to return descriptive error messages instead of boolean; (2) Verify row counts in updateTodoStatus and deleteTodo to detect non-existent IDs; (3) Add try-catch blocks for database operations with meaningful error messages.

Enhance sanitizeInput function to include ampersand encoding and consider using a battle-tested library like DOMPurify for comprehensive XSS prevention. The current implementation only handles basic cases.

Add database indexes for performance: (1) CREATE INDEX idx_todos_created_at ON todos(created_at DESC) for getAllTodos sorting; (2) CREATE INDEX idx_user_todos_user_id ON user_todos(user_id) for getTodosByUser; (3) Consider full-text search indexes for searchTodos using PostgreSQL GIN indexes.
Define custom error classes (TodoNotFoundError, InvalidTodoInputError) for domain-specific errors to improve error handling and make it easier for consumers to handle different error scenarios.
